result.area_summary: The cmd-audit slice is in strong shape on its headline invariants: run_audit claims its CancelToken before the six-way prefetch, latches a dead session via its own reauth_fatal flag inside the dispatch_capped call site, counts unscored principals and unresolved resource indexes into `degraded`, and gates the CacheKind::Audit write on `run_is_cacheable` (exhaustively unit-tested). The sequential bulk driver run_bulk_seq is unit-tested for ordering, cancel-before-first-item and stop-on-reauth-fatal, and SP-only rows are pinned non-selectable by the GUI tests. Weaknesses are concentrated at the edges: the adaptive throttle re-anchors its halving window on every 429 so a sustained storm halves the cap exactly once; the readiness scope probe keeps a hardcoded CAE list that has drifted from the capabilities catalog (group_membership probed non-CAE, policy_write/sync probed but never catalogued); the redundant-permissions Fix silently drops values its Exchange veto blocks while its own doc says they land in `skipped`; score_one swallows a failed SP lookup and can then cache a Scoped verdict that was never reconciled; and several doc comments still narrate the retired `reset()` model. audit.rs at 2011 lines mixes orchestration, six prefetchers, scoring, cache and three export writers and should split.

findings.title: ConcurrencyThrottle halves only once under sustained 429 pressure because the window re-anchors on every event
findings.rationale: `HALVE_WINDOW_SECS` is documented as the 'Minimum seconds between cap halvings', but `*last = Some(now)` runs before the `within_window` early return, so a suppressed event still moves the anchor. With 4-8 lanes each receiving 429s more often than every 2s (the normal shape of a Graph throttle storm) `within` is true for every event after the first, and the cap goes 8→4 and stays there — the 'degrade to per-object reads / floor at 1' behaviour never engages. The existing paused-clock test only fires bursts at a single instant and then advances past the window, so it cannot see this.
findings.proposal: Track two instants: `last_throttle` (updated on every event; drives the recovery quiet check) and `last_halved` (updated only when `next < prev`; drives the halving window). Add a `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` that fires `on_throttle` every 1s for 10s on `new(8)` and asserts the limit reaches `MIN_CONCURRENCY`.

findings.title: Readiness scope probe keeps a hardcoded CAE list that has drifted from the capabilities catalog (group_membership probed non-CAE)
findings.rationale: The catalog carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")` (capabilities.rs:308) and `AppState::ensure_group_member_token` acquires it with `cae = true` (state.rs:630-645), but this list omits `group_membership`, so the readiness page pre-warms a non-CAE token for a Graph scope set. state.rs:563-568 states the invariant this breaks: 'cae MUST match the CAE-ness of the adapter that later consumes the same scope set: the token cache key omits CAE-ness, so a non-CAE pre-warm would make a new_cae adapter reuse a non-CAE token'. The same list also names `sync` and `policy_write`, which no catalog entry probes, showing it is maintained by hand and nothing pins it.
findings.proposal: Move CAE-ness next to the scope set: have `AppState::consent_scopes_for` return `(Vec<String>, bool /*cae*/)` (or add a `cae: bool` column to a small feature table) and make both `ensure_scoped_token` wrappers and `probe_scope` read it. Delete the `is_graph` match. Add a unit test asserting every catalog `scope_feature` resolves through `consent_scopes_for`.

findings.title: Redundant-permissions Fix silently drops values whose covering permission is vetoed — doc says they land in `skipped`, and the UI then clears the Fix button
findings.rationale: The handler's fail-closed comment (remediation.rs:373-377) promises: 'skipping it costs the operator a re-run once Exchange answers, and the value shows up in `skipped` saying so'. But when every covering permission is vetoed (`Err(_) => HashMap::new()` at :401 for a non-Exchange-admin, or a transient Exchange failure via `.unwrap_or_default()` at :399) the loop hits `continue` without `skipped.push`. The command returns `Ok { removed: [], skipped: [] }`; `RedundantPermsAction` (web-rs row.rs:377-395) then toasts 'Removed 0 redundant permissions' and calls `on_done`, which `retain`s the RemoveRedundantPermissions button away while the finding and the live permission remain. An operator without Exchange RBAC rights can never see why the Fix did nothing.
findings.proposal: In `plan_redundant_removals`, collect the pre-veto broaders first; if non-empty but the post-veto set is empty, push the value into `skipped` (or a new `vetoed: Vec<String>` on `RedundantPermissionsOutcome` with a reason string). In the UI, only fire `on_done` when `removed` is non-empty, and render the veto reason ('could not confirm the covering permission is org-wide — Exchange unavailable'). Add a planner test for the all-vetoed case.

findings.title: score_one swallows a failed SP lookup, skips the org-wide reconciliation, and the run still caches as a clean complete scan
findings.rationale: When the lean lookup fails (Graph 5xx after retries, or a task that runs after the LRU seed was evicted — `seed_lean_sps_from_index` caps at the bucket size), `sp` is `None` but scoring continues: Rule 4 (disabled SP) and Rule 3 (admin consent) lose their input, and — more importantly — `orgwide` is empty so `resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached` can return a `Scoped { Rbac }` verdict that is never reconciled against a surviving org-wide grant. That is exactly the under-report the AuditCoverageGap::GraphAppRoleAssignments doc (dto/audit.rs:141-146) calls out, yet here nothing is added to `degraded`, so the run passes `run_is_cacheable` and is served from cache as authoritative. Contrast `ResourceResolver.unresolved`, which exists precisely to flag the equivalent hole for resource indexes.
findings.proposal: Either return `Err(err.into())` from score_one on a failed SP lookup (it classifies as Transient → `unscored` → `PerPrincipalScoring`, and a dead session is caught by the same match), or add an `sp_unresolved: AtomicBool` to ScoreCtx and push a new `AuditCoverageGap::ServicePrincipalLookup` when set. In both cases skip the Exchange probe when `sp` is `None` (reconciliation is impossible, so the reduced weight must not be awarded).

findings.title: SSO claims-mapping (Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration) and provisioning read (Synchronization.Read.All) have no capabilities-catalog entry, so readiness never checks them and 403s cannot splice a remediation
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md: 'three auth planes share one capabilities catalog — add an entry instead of a hardcoded role string'. The SSO claims-mapping flow acquires `policy_write` via `ensure_policy_write_token` (two call sites in commands/sso/mod.rs) and the Graph client carries a `sync_token`, but `CAPABILITIES` has no entry whose `scope_feature` is `policy_write` or `sync`. The readiness checklist therefore cannot tell an operator that claims-mapping needs `Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration` plus Cloud Application Administrator, and a 403 on those paths has no `capability_key` for `graph_err::forbidden_remediation`. The probe list even names both features, so the probing code exists and simply has nothing to attach to.
findings.proposal: Add two `Capability` entries in azapptoolkit-core::capabilities: `sso_claims_mapping` (plane EntraDirectory, roles Cloud Application Administrator / Application Administrator / Global Administrator, scopes ["Policy.ReadWrite.ApplicationConfiguration"], `scope_feature: Some("policy_write")`) and `provisioning_read` (`scope_feature: Some("sync")`). Splice `forbidden_remediation(&err, "sso_claims_mapping")` into the two sso 403 paths. Add a test that every feature key `consent_scopes_for` accepts appears as some catalog `scope_feature` and vice versa, so the two tables cannot drift again.

findings.title: bulk_remove_expired_credentials pages the whole tenant even for an explicit selection, filters with O(n·m) Vec::contains, and the 10 000 cap can silently drop a selected app
findings.rationale: The Findings pane's 'Fix all N' and the App Registrations bulk bar always pass `Some(object_ids)` (a handful to a few hundred ids), yet the command still walks every page of `/applications` — tens of seconds on a large tenant — before discarding all but the selection. `ids.contains` is a linear scan per app (10 000 × selection size). And the comment's 'where the cap cannot matter' is wrong: a selected app beyond the 10 000th page position is dropped from `apps`, so `apps_scanned` is short and the UI has no signal (the flag is bound to `_truncated`). The literal `10_000` also duplicates `applications::APPS_MAX`, which audit.rs:84 uses by name.
findings.proposal: When `object_ids` is `Some`, fetch exactly those apps with the same `$select` via the existing `$batch` GET helper (falling back to per-id `get_application` through `batch_or_serial`), skipping the tenant walk entirely; keep the walk only for the tenant-wide sweep and surface `truncated` on `BulkRemoveExpiredResult` for that path. Use `APPS_MAX` instead of the literal and a `HashSet<&str>` for the retain.

findings.title: Bulk expired-credential sweep busts both tenant-wide indexes (invalidate_app_lists) for a credential-only mutation; the per-app fix uses the tiered invalidation
findings.rationale: applications/cache.rs:140-147 documents why credential mutations must use `invalidate_app_credentials`: it 'deliberately leaves the shared SP pairing index, the app-name search index, the Enterprise Apps list, and every mailbox-scope verdict intact… dropping them forces the next list visit to re-enumerate every app and every service principal (tens of seconds on a large tenant) for a change that touched neither.' `remediate_remove_expired_credentials` (remediation.rs:97-99) follows that rule; the bulk sweep of the same mutation does not, so after every sweep the operator pays a full SP-index + app-name-index rebuild.
findings.proposal: Replace the `invalidate_app_lists` call with a loop over `summaries.iter().filter(|s| !s.removed_key_ids.is_empty())` calling `invalidate_app_credentials(&state.cache, &tenant_id, &s.object_id)` (or add an `invalidate_app_credentials_many(cache, tenant, &[object_id])` that drops the shared keys once and the per-app detail keys per id). Extend `repo_invariants/cache.rs` to pin that no credential-only command calls `invalidate_app_lists`.

findings.title: Exchange mailbox-scoping unavailability (no Exchange client, or breaker tripped) is invisible in the run result, the workbench and every export
findings.rationale: By design a non-Exchange-admin gets org-wide weight for every mail permission (never under-report), and that trade-off should stay. But the consequence for the operator is that apps already scoped via RBAC are listed as Critical 'Org-wide mailbox access' with a 'Scope…' Fix that will fail, the healthy 'Mailbox access scoped' group is empty, and the run is cached and exported as complete. `coverage_sentences` (audit.rs:636-642) already adds a caveat when the sign-in report was unavailable; the analogous, higher-impact caveat for mailbox scoping does not exist, and `AuditRunResult` carries no field for it. Nothing in web-rs/views/audit_view or security_view mentions Exchange availability (grep).
findings.proposal: Add `mailbox_scoping_resolved: bool` (`#[serde(default = true)]`-style) to `AuditRunResult`, `AuditExportCoverage` and `CachedAuditRun`, set false when `exo` is `None` or `exo_tripped` is set at the end of the run; add a sentence in `coverage_sentences` ('Mailbox scoping could not be resolved — org-wide mailbox findings may include applications already confined via Exchange RBAC; sign in as an Exchange Administrator to refine') and a Callout in the Org-wide mailbox finding group. Keep it out of `degraded` so the run stays cacheable, matching the sign-in precedent.

findings.title: Split commands/audit.rs (2011 lines) into a directory module by concern
findings.evidence:
126:#[tauri::command]  pub async fn run_audit            (to ~475)
476..540: cancel_audit / invalidate_audit_cache / get_cached_audit
542:#[tauri::command]  pub async fn save_audit_to_file  + cached_run_coverage, coverage_sentences, severity_summary, audit_to_json (667), audit_to_html (702), html_escape, export_audit_csv (788)
854:// ---------------- internals ----------------
860:struct ScoreCtx  … 914/952/1007/1070/1137/1182: six prefetch_* fns
1238:fn score_sp_only  1312:fn sp_audit_candidates  1329:struct ResourceResolver  1437:async fn resolve_permissions  1483:async fn score_one
1615:#[cfg(test)] mod tests (≈400 lines)
findings.rationale: The file interleaves five independent concerns: run orchestration and cancellation, the six tenant-wide prefetchers (~380 lines), per-principal scoring (ScoreCtx, ResourceResolver, resolve_permissions, score_one, score_sp_only, ~370 lines), the cache entry (CachedAuditRun, key, run_is_cacheable, get_cached_audit) and three export writers (~310 lines). Each has its own invariants (documented at length inline) and its own test group. `commands/exchange/` already proves the directory-module shape works here, and `repo_invariants/sources.rs` walks subdirectories and skips a sibling `tests.rs`, so the source-scanning pins keep working unchanged.
findings.proposal: Create `commands/audit/{mod.rs, prefetch.rs, score.rs, cache.rs, export.rs, tests.rs}`: `mod.rs` keeps run_audit/cancel_audit and re-exports the four commands so `lib.rs`'s `generate_handler![]` paths do not change; `prefetch.rs` takes the six `prefetch_*` + `derive_orgwide_mail_scopes`; `score.rs` takes ScoreCtx, ResourceResolver, resolve_permissions, score_one, score_sp_only, sp_audit_candidates; `cache.rs` takes CachedAuditRun, audit_cache_key, run_is_cacheable, invalidate_audit_cache, get_cached_audit; `export.rs` takes save_audit_to_file and the writers. Move each test group next to its subject. No behaviour change; run `just verify`.

findings.title: No source-level pin that the CacheKind::Audit write is guarded by run_is_cacheable
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md states 'a cancelled/truncated/degraded run is never cached'. `run_is_cacheable` is exhaustively unit-tested (`only_a_complete_undegraded_run_is_cacheable`), but that pins the predicate, not its use: a refactor that moves the `cache.put` out of the `if` (or adds a second put, e.g. for a 'partial snapshot') compiles and passes every test. `repo_invariants/cache.rs` today only checks the cache-only *read* proves the session (line 580). The slice's other rules — claim-before-await, dead-session gate per call site — each have a source-scan pin; this one does not.
findings.proposal: Add a test in `repo_invariants/cache.rs`: read `commands/audit.rs` (or the future `audit/` directory), find every `.put(CacheKind::Audit` occurrence, and assert the nearest enclosing `if` condition (scan backwards to the previous `{` at the same brace depth) contains `run_is_cacheable(`; assert at least one occurrence exists so the rule cannot pass vacuously.

findings.title: Stale `reset()` narrative in run_bulk_seq's doc and the architecture deep-dive; cancel.rs cites a test that no longer exists
findings.rationale: `CancelFlag` no longer has a `reset()` — state.rs:44-49 explains it was removed because it was 'a destructive write on state a concurrent run was still reading', and `repo_invariants/cancel.rs` opens with 'Replaces the old "call reset() at the top" rule'. Three places still teach the retired model, and cancel.rs points at `the_audit_claims_its_token_before_the_prefetch`, which does not exist anywhere in the tree (grep) — it was generalised into `every_long_running_command_claims_before_its_first_await`. A reader following the doc will look for a `reset()` and a test that are both gone.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the run_bulk_seq doc line to 'The caller claims a `CancelToken` once, before its first await (pinned by `repo_invariants::cancel`), and passes it down'; update the arch doc sentence to 'They `claim()` a token + poll it'; change the cancel.rs intra-doc link to `every_long_running_command_claims_before_its_first_await`.

findings.title: FanOutTicker::tick's doc claims count and cap are read under one lock — they are not — and progress events can arrive out of order
findings.rationale: The cap is read after `drop(guard)`, and `current` is an atomic the mutex never protected anyway, so the comment describes a guarantee the code does not provide. Separately, every caller (`audit.rs:335-346`, bulk delete/grant/sweep) emits *after* `tick()` returns and outside any lock, so two tasks can tick 5 then 6 and emit 6 then 5; `use_progress_stream` (web-rs hooks) does `progress.set(Some(p))` unconditionally, so the bar can step backwards — the very skew the comment says is prevented. A `tokio::sync::Mutex<usize>` is also heavier than needed for a counter.
findings.proposal: Replace `done: Arc<Mutex<usize>>` with `Arc<AtomicUsize>` and `fetch_add(1) + 1`; fix the comment to say the pair is best-effort. Make `use_progress_stream` (or a small `AuditProgress::newer_than`) ignore an event whose `done` is lower than the current one for the same `total`, so the bar is monotonic per run.

findings.title: Demo registers a fixture for `export_audit_csv`, a command that no longer exists on the IPC boundary
findings.rationale: `export_audit_csv` was demoted to a `pub(crate)` helper (audit.rs doc: 'leaving an unreachable entry point on the IPC boundary'), and no binding invokes it, yet the Pages demo still mocks it and docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:111 lists it among the infallible `invoke()` commands that need fixtures. `demo_fixture_coverage.rs` checks only that every infallible invoke has a fixture, not the reverse, so the dead fixture is invisible to CI.
findings.proposal: Delete the `mock_ok("export_audit_csv", …)` block and the mention in release-updater-demo.md:111. Optionally add the reverse assertion to `demo_fixture_coverage.rs` (every mocked command name appears in some `invoke`/`invoke_result` call in bindings), which would also catch future leftovers.

findings.title: premium_feature_err hardcodes 'Ask a Global Administrator' while the catalog's admin_consent entry names Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator
findings.rationale: The same file's `forbidden_remediation` exists so that 'Adding a privileged feature means adding a catalog entry, never a hardcoded role string', and AGENTS.md repeats the rule. This message is the one remaining hardcoded role string on a 403 path in the slice, and it is narrower than the catalog's own answer (a Privileged Role Administrator can also grant the consent).
findings.proposal: Compose the consent branch from the catalog: `let roles = capability("admin_consent").map(|c| c.role_names().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" or "))` and interpolate it, or append `capability("admin_consent").remediation`. Add a small test that the message names both roles.

findings.title: run_audit emits no progress until the six tenant-wide prefetches finish, so the longest phase of a large scan shows only a spinner
findings.rationale: The inline comment at :160-166 says the prefetch 'is the longest phase of a large run' and 'the most likely moment for an operator to press Cancel'. `security_view.rs:180-183` renders the progress block only once `progress` is `Some`, so for that entire phase the operator sees a disabled button with a tiny spinner and a Cancel button, with no indication of what is happening or that the app is alive. Progress events are best-effort and cheap (`emit_progress`), so a preparatory event costs nothing.
findings.proposal: Before the `join!`, emit `AuditProgress { done: 0, total: 0, current_app: Some("Reading tenant-wide directory data…".into()), in_flight_cap: meter.limit(), cancelled: false }`; the view already guards `p.total > 0` for the percentage, so it renders an indeterminate bar with that label. Optionally emit one more when `apps` lands with the real `total`.

findings.title: Terminal bulk-progress events report `done: total` even when the run was cancelled or halted early
findings.rationale: After a Cancel at item 3 of 10, or a dead-session halt, the final event tells the UI '10 / 10 (cancelled)'. `BulkProgressRow` (bulk_action_bar.rs:227) renders `p.done / p.total`, so the bar snaps to 100% for a run that processed a fraction of the selection — the same 'partial reads as complete' shape the surrounding code is careful about elsewhere. `bulk_remove_expired_credentials` emits no terminal event at all, so the three fan-out paths and the sequential driver disagree on the contract.
findings.proposal: Emit `done: outcomes.len()` (sequential) / the collected count (fan-outs) in the terminal event, keep `total` as the denominator, and give `bulk_remove_expired_credentials` the same terminal event. Extend `processes_every_item_and_reports_progress_before_each` / `a_cancel_before_the_first_item_processes_nothing` to assert the terminal `done` equals the processed count.

minor_nits: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:6-8 — module doc says the expired-credential sweep is 'the exception' that runs its own concurrent loop; bulk_delete_applications (:311) and bulk_grant_permissions (:410) also fan out through dispatch_capped.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:759-760 — bulk_add_owner doc claims it reuses 'add_application_owner's core'; no such core exists — both it and owners.rs:14-24 call client.add_owner directly.

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:79-82 — BulkOutcome impls for AppRemovalSummary and BulkGrantOutcome are never exercised (both outcomes are produced only on dispatch_capped paths; run_bulk_seq is the sole consumer of the trait).
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/bulk.rs:172 — `Some(10_000)` literal duplicates applications::APPS_MAX, which audit.rs:84 references by name.

crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/bulk.rs:56 — BulkProgress.in_flight_cap doc says it is `None` for the bulk-credential/create/delete flows; the credential sweep, delete and grant now send `Some(meter.limit())`.
docs/architecture/release-updater-demo.md:111 — lists `export_audit_csv` among the infallible invoke() commands that need demo fixtures; it is no longer a command.

result.coverage_notes: All seven slice files were read end to end: audit.rs (2011 lines, in six chunks), bulk.rs (1235), remediation.rs (651), readiness.rs (457), dispatch.rs (260), throttle.rs (291), graph_err.rs (161). Also read fully: docs/architecture/audit-findings-and-remediation.md, tests/repo_invariants/cancel.rs and fanout.rs, and the head of sources.rs. Cross-checked by targeted grep/sed (not read fully): state.rs (CancelFlag, consent_scopes_for, ensure_* probes), core/capabilities.rs (catalog keys and admin_consent entry), dto/audit.rs and dto/bulk.rs, applications/cache.rs (invalidation helpers), exchange/mail_scopes.rs (resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached), graph client list_applications_all and seed_lean_sps_from_index, web-rs audit_view/{controller,row}.rs, security_view.rs, bulk_action_bar.rs, hooks/use_progress_stream.rs, demo/mod.rs, GUI tests security_audit.rs/security_findings.rs (confirmed SP-only rows are pinned non-selectable and routed to SP cores, so that rule was not reported as unpinned). Per the ground rules no cargo build/test/clippy was run; the throttle bug and the redundant-permissions veto path were verified by reading control flow, not by executing the tokio tests.

result.area_summary: The cmd-apps slice is in good shape where the repo's documented contracts are pinned by tests: tenant-scoped keys, the tiered invalidation (`invalidate_app_lists` / `_credentials` / `_details` / `_detail_state`), generation watches on the pinned indexes, the full-collection PATCH contract for `appRoles` / `oauth2PermissionScopes` (live re-read, disable-then-remove, raw-JSON round-trip), and the client-secret window (default 180, cap 730) are all implemented as documented and unit-tested. The weak spots are the paths those pins do not reach: three shared cores (`create_application_core`, both grant cores) return `Err` after a real Graph write so the command layer skips invalidation (retry of a "failed" create makes a duplicate app); `get_application_detail` caches a degraded permission resolution that shows granted permissions as not granted for the 60-minute TTL; `global_search` answers from the corpus without proving the session and the invariant that should catch it only scans command bodies and treats `graph_for(` as proof; `list_app_role_resources` has no invalidation although `app_roles.rs` mutates exactly what it lists; and `list_credential_expirations` stores a tenant-wide scan unguarded, the race the doc records as fixed elsewhere. Handler-level tests exist only for `add_password_core`; every other mutation's invalidation tier is review-checked.

findings.title: create_application returns Err after the app registration was already created, so no cache is invalidated and a retry creates a duplicate
findings.rationale: caching-and-search.md's rule for multi-step mutations is "a partial success is a real write — invalidate, gated on 'something actually changed'", which `downgrade_application_permission_core`, `remove_expired_passwords` and the bulk commands obey. Here `POST /applications` succeeds, then a 403/429 from `ensure_service_principal` (or `add_password`) propagates via `?`; the command returns Err and `invalidate_app_lists` never runs. `apps_pairing`, `app_name_index` and `search_corpus` are pinned (LRU cannot evict them) with a 60-minute TTL, so the App Registrations list and global search do not show the new app, the operator sees only an error, and the natural retry creates a second registration with the same display name (Entra allows duplicates). `bulk_create` avoids this only because it passes `..Default::default()` (no SP, no secret).
findings.proposal: Give `create_application_core` the shape `downgrade_application_permission_core` already has: return `Ok((CreateApplicationResult, Option<UiError>))` (or add `error: Option<UiError>` to `CreateApplicationResult`) once `create_application` has landed, collecting SP/secret failures instead of `?`-ing them; in the command, call `invalidate_app_lists` whenever `application` exists and then surface the error. Update `bulk.rs:570` and `restore.rs:218` callers (both already tolerate per-item errors). Add a wiremock handler test (POST /applications 201, POST /servicePrincipals 403) asserting `apps_pairing`/`app_name_index` are dropped and the error is returned.

findings.title: get_application_detail caches a degraded permission resolution: a transient failure resolving one resource SP marks all of that resource's permissions as not granted for the 60-minute TTL
findings.rationale: `.ok().flatten()` collapses `Err(429/5xx/dead token)` into the same `None` as `Ok(None)` (resource SP genuinely absent). With `live_sp == None` both join closures return `None`, so every `ResolvedPermission` for that resource carries `runtime_assignment_id: None` / `runtime_grant_id: None`, which the Permissions tab renders as not granted and offers to grant. The detail is then stored unconditionally under `app_detail_key` for the Lists TTL. AGENTS.md says a degraded run is never cached nor shown as all-clear; here a permission that IS granted is shown as absent, and only the operator's manual Refresh clears it. `resolve_resource_sp` itself caches only `Ok`, so the graph layer got this right and the command layer undid it.
findings.proposal: Make `resolve_required_resource_access` return `(Vec<ResolvedPermission>, bool /*degraded*/)` by keeping `Result<Option<SP>>` per resource and setting `degraded` on any `Err`; in `get_application_detail` skip `state.cache.put` when degraded, and add `#[serde(default)] resolution_degraded: bool` to `ApplicationDetail` so the tab can show a `Callout` ("Permission grants could not be fully resolved; Refresh to retry"). Unit-test the resolver with one `Err` resource: rows still returned, flag set.

findings.title: global_search (and prefetch_search_corpus / get_directory_index_status) answer from cache without proving the session, and the invariant that pins the rule cannot see them
findings.rationale: session.rs documents that a read-through command whose hit path returns before a token is fetched must call `prove_tenant_session` first, because otherwise the `tenant_id` argument alone decides whose directory data is returned (tenant switch mid-flight; dead session with data caches kept). `graph_for` only constructs token adapters (no token is acquired until a request), so on a warm corpus `global_search` returns the previous session's app/SP names having proven nothing. The invariant passes vacuously: the `cache.get_typed` lives inside `search_corpus`, not the command body, and `graph_for(` is accepted as a proof. `prefetch_search_corpus` (search.rs:235-236) and `get_directory_index_status` (mod.rs:108-109, via `sp_index_cached`) have the same shape, with less to leak. Sign-out sweeps the caches, so the exposure is the mid-flight switch and dead-session cases, which is why this is medium rather than high.
findings.proposal: Add `crate::commands::session::prove_tenant_session(&state, &tenant_id)?;` as the first statement of `global_search`, `prefetch_search_corpus` and `get_directory_index_status`. Harden the invariant: extend `first_cache_read` to also match the cached-accessor names (`sp_index_cached(`, `app_name_index_cached(`, `indexes_cached(`, `search_corpus(`, `sp_index_hit(`, `load_gallery_corpus(`), and drop `graph_for(`/`*_for(` from `SESSION_PROOFS` (a factory call is not a proof); bump `KNOWN_CACHE_READING_COMMANDS` accordingly.

findings.title: grant_single_permission_core and grant_admin_consent_core return Err after real writes (manifest PATCH, SP creation) so the command layer never invalidates
findings.rationale: In the single-grant core the `requiredResourceAccess` PATCH lands, then `ensure_service_principal` (creates an SP, a new Enterprise App row) or `resolve_resource_sp` fails with `?`. The command receives Err and busts nothing: the cached detail shows the old manifest, and a newly created SP is missing from `sp_index`/enterprise/search for the TTL. In the admin-consent core the SP is created and then the idempotency `try_join` fails (a 403 on `oauth2PermissionGrants` for an operator without `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All` is realistic); same outcome. The repo already solved this exact shape in `downgrade_application_permission_core` and its doc comment explains why; the two grant cores predate it.
findings.proposal: Adopt the `(outcome, Option<UiError>)` return in both grant cores: once the manifest PATCH or `ensure_service_principal` has landed, collect later errors instead of `?`, and have `grant_single_permission` / `grant_admin_consent` (and the bulk/restore callers) invalidate on `manifest_changed || sp_created` before surfacing the error. Mirror the two `downgrade` tests for these cores with wiremock.

findings.title: list_app_role_resources is cached with "no mutation-driven invalidation" although the App roles tab mutates exactly what it lists
findings.rationale: `list_tenant_app_role_resources` returns tenant-owned SPs exposing an enabled Application role plus a role count. `upsert_enterprise_app_role`/`delete_enterprise_app_role` change that set (first Application role added, last one disabled), and `create_application`/`delete_application` add or remove the SP. None of them drop `{tenant}|app_role_resources`, so the Grant-access picker's "Tenant app registrations" group (permission_picker.rs:119) omits a freshly published API, keeps a deleted app, and shows stale counts for up to 60 minutes. The graph crate already busts its own `resource:` prefix on the same writes for the same reason (applications.rs:622-625); the command-side list was not given the same treatment.
findings.proposal: Move `app_role_resources_key` into `applications/cache.rs`; drop it inside `invalidate_app_lists`, and add a targeted `cache.invalidate(CacheKind::Lists, &app_role_resources_key(tenant))` on the Ok path of `upsert_enterprise_app_role` and `delete_enterprise_app_role`. Extend `detail_cache_tests` with an assertion that `invalidate_app_lists` drops it. Fix the doc comment.

findings.title: list_credential_expirations stores a tenant-wide scan unguarded, the store-after-invalidate race the doc records as fixed for the other list caches
findings.rationale: A `remove_password`/`add_password` landing during the multi-second `/applications` scan calls `invalidate_app_credentials`, which drops `credential_expirations`; the scan then stores its pre-mutation snapshot, so the Credential Expiry tab and the Home tile show a removed secret as still expiring (or miss a new one) until the 60-minute TTL. The entry is not pinned, so LRU can evict it under pressure, but nothing else corrects it. The guard invariant only counts `put_index(`/`put_typed_index(`, so a plain `put` after a tenant-wide scan is invisible to it.
findings.proposal: Capture `let watch = state.cache.generation_for(CacheKind::Lists, &cache_key);` before `list_applications_all` and store via `state.cache.put_index_if_current(watch, &rows)` (this is a full-directory-scan entry, exactly what the doc says pinning is for; the bucket already pins `apps_pairing`). Extend the invariant to flag a `cache.put(` in any command body that also contains `list_applications_all(`/`list_service_principals_index(`.

findings.title: list_applications_with_pairing bypasses the SP-index single-flight gate and has no gate of its own; two frontend surfaces call it
findings.rationale: On a cold tenant, Home mounting and the operator clicking App Registrations before it returns runs two full `/applications` scans and two `/servicePrincipals` scans (tens of seconds each on a large tenant), and a concurrent gated reader (Enterprise Apps, MI list, search prewarm) runs a third SP scan because `state.single_flight(sp_index_key)` never sees this caller. The same file's sibling helpers were explicitly rewritten to avoid this. The dedicated `sp_index_watch` helper exists only to serve this bypass.
findings.proposal: Replace the `None` arm with `futures::future::try_join(client.list_applications_all(query, Some(APPS_MAX)), cache::sp_index_cached(&state, &client, &tenant_id))` (keeps the concurrency, gains the gate and the correctly-keyed watch; `sp_index_watch` and the `Some(cached_index)` arm become unnecessary since `sp_index_cached` hit-checks). Wrap the miss path in `state.single_flight(&cache_key)` with a post-lock re-check, as `search_corpus` does.

findings.title: Certificate upload accepts any base64 body: a pasted private key or cert+key bundle is sent to Graph, and the expiry is whatever the operator typed
findings.evidence:
credentials.rs:249-259
/// ... Performs minimal validation:
/// strips headers/whitespace and confirms the remainder is valid base64.
fn normalize_cert_blob(input: &str) -> std::result::Result<String, String> {
    let stripped: String = input
        .lines()
        .filter(|line| !line.trim_start().starts_with("-----"))
credentials.rs:117-118
        key: key_b64,
        end_date_time: input.end_date_time,
Cargo.lock: `x509-parser` is already a dependency of `p12-keystore` 0.2.1 and `rcgen` (both direct deps of src-tauri).
findings.rationale: The armour filter strips every `-----` line regardless of label, so the common openssl output that holds `CERTIFICATE` followed by `PRIVATE KEY` decodes as one valid base64 string and the private-key bytes are transmitted to Graph before it rejects the blob; a lone `[PEM BEGIN PRIVATE KEY]` paste behaves the same. Nothing parses the DER, so `end_date_time` is never checked against the certificate's notAfter, the row's soonest-expiry and the audit's expiring-credential finding can disagree with the real certificate, and the operator gets no thumbprint to confirm what they uploaded. For a security-critical app whose own generate path zeroizes private keys, the upload path should refuse to forward one.
findings.proposal: In `normalize_cert_blob`: reject when any `-----BEGIN` label is not `CERTIFICATE` (specifically `PRIVATE KEY`, `RSA PRIVATE KEY`, `ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY`, `PKCS7`), take only the first CERTIFICATE block, and parse the DER with `x509_parser::parse_x509_certificate` (add it as a direct dep at the version already in the lock). Return `(key_b64, not_after, sha1_thumbprint)`; default `end_date_time` to notAfter, reject an operator value later than it, and set `custom_key_identifier` via `core::thumbprint::hex_upper`. Add tests for the key-paste and bundle cases.

findings.title: GUID search swallows probe failures, so a throttled or dead-session lookup renders as "No matches"
findings.rationale: The module's own contract is that search must never silently omit. On the GUID path a 429, a 403 (operator without SP read), or a dead token on all four probes is indistinguishable from a genuine 404, and the frontend has no signal to show, so an admin pasting an appId from the portal concludes the app does not exist. `Err(GraphError::NotFound)` is the only error that means "not there".
findings.proposal: Distinguish `Err(GraphError::NotFound(_))` (a real miss) from other errors in the GUID branch; add `#[serde(default)] pub lookup_degraded: bool` to `GlobalSearchResults` (additive, like the five existing defaults) set when any probe failed with a non-404, and render it through the same `cap_notice` slot ("Directory lookup failed; results may be incomplete"). Unit-test `assemble_guid_hits` with an `Err(Throttled)` input.

findings.title: No handler-level tests exist for any core except add_password_core, although the seam and fixtures for them already exist
findings.rationale: The tiering decisions in this slice (sp_created -> lists vs detail-state in both grant commands; `remove_expired_passwords` invalidating only when something was removed; `set_application_owners` likewise; `downgrade` invalidating on partial success; `create_application` after a partial create) are exactly the review-only rules the credentials.rs comment describes, and two of them are wrong today (findings 1 and 4). The three tests in `handler_tests` are a ready template.
findings.proposal: Add a `handler_tests` module to applications/mod.rs and permissions.rs (and owners.rs) using `AppState::for_test` + wiremock, one triple per core: success busts the expected tier and keeps the indexes; failure busts nothing; partial success (first write 2xx, later write 4xx) busts and returns the error. Seed with the existing `seed()` helper pattern.

findings.title: create_application_core computes the initial secret lifetime with its own rule (no clamp, no 24-month cap, 0 days accepted), diverging from resolve_password_window
findings.rationale: Three copies of the 180-day default and only one of the 1..=730 clamp. `initial_secret_lifetime_days: Option<u32>` accepts `Some(0)` (end == now, Graph 400, which then trips finding 1) and `Some(3650)` (a 10-year secret from a path whose sibling caps at 24 months). Today the create dialog never sends `initial_secret_*` (only bulk/restore reach the core, with `None`), so this is latent rather than live, but the seam is a public IPC argument.
findings.proposal: Make `resolve_password_window` `pub(super)` (or extract `clamp_secret_lifetime_days`) and have `create_application_core` call `client.add_password_window(&application.id, name, None, end)` with the clamped end; delete `GraphClient::add_password` once callerless. One table test covering 0 / 9999.

findings.title: Search corpus reports SP-index truncation but discards the app-registration index's own truncation
findings.rationale: `app_name_index_cached` is capped at `APPS_MAX` (10 000) too. A tenant with more registrations than service principals (automation-heavy tenants accumulate registrations without SPs) has its app-reg half truncated while `corpus_truncated` stays false, so the dropdown says "No matches" for a registration that exists; the doc calls both caps "must not drift" and the SP one is already surfaced for exactly this reason.
findings.proposal: Compute `index_truncated: sps.len() >= SP_INDEX_MAX || apps.len() >= APPS_MAX` (rename the field; the DTO field `corpus_truncated` already abstracts the source), or return the `truncated` bool from `list_application_index_named` and carry it through `app_name_index_cached`.

findings.title: PermissionKind -> manifest entry-type mapping is written three times in permissions.rs, one copy being the helper extracted to avoid that
findings.rationale: `entry_type_for` was "split out so the mapping is testable" yet `declare_app_permission` re-inlines an identical match with identical code and message; a future change to the message or code (the frontend can branch on `code`) would need to be made twice.
findings.proposal: `declare_app_permission`: `let entry_type = entry_type_for(kind)?;`. `remove_declared_permission`: `let entry_type = entry_type_for(kind).ok();` (Unknown legitimately maps to None there).

findings.title: caching-and-search.md says invalidate_app_lists drops "seven" things; the code drops nine, and AGENTS.md names three tiers where there are four
findings.evidence:

`invalidate_app_lists` drops **seven** things together: the apps-pairing, enterprise, `sp_index`,
`app_name_index`, and `search_corpus` keys, plus — transitively — the per-app detail cache
(`invalidate_app_details`) and the cached audit run

- **Invalidate caches only on `Ok`** (`invalidate_app_lists` / `invalidate_app_credentials` / `invalidate_app_details`)

findings.rationale: The same paragraph records that "two reviews independently mis-read this as a missing invalidation because earlier versions of this doc listed only the four list keys"; the list has drifted again in the same direction. The fourth tier (`invalidate_app_detail_state`) is the one most mutations in this slice call and is absent from the AGENTS.md sentence.
findings.proposal: Update the doc to enumerate all nine (or say "every key in `invalidate_app_lists`" and link the function), add `invalidate_app_detail_state` to AGENTS.md:101, and back the list with a test in `detail_cache_tests` that asserts the exact set of Lists keys dropped so the doc can cite it.

findings.title: progress.rs doc comment says tests can pass a tauri::test::mock_app() handle, but the tauri test feature is not enabled and was deliberately dropped
findings.rationale: A contributor following the progress.rs comment will re-add `tauri/test` and reintroduce the Windows breakage the credentials.rs comment records. The generic parameter is harmless but its stated justification is false.
findings.proposal: Reword to state that the generic keeps the helper testable with a caller-defined `Runtime` and that `tauri/test` is intentionally not enabled (link `d8d293e`), or drop the generic and take `&AppHandle`.

findings.title: permissions.rs is 1417 lines spanning six concerns; applications/ was already split the same way
findings.rationale: The catalog picker, the pure manifest helpers (`remove_declared_access`, `declare_resource_access`, `swap_declared_role`), and three multi-step Graph orchestrations with different invalidation shapes share one file, which is why the three-way `PermissionKind` duplication and the `(outcome, error)` vs `?` asymmetry between the cores went unnoticed. The glob re-export pattern needed to keep `generate_handler!` paths stable is already proven in `applications/mod.rs`.
findings.proposal: Split into `permissions/{catalog,manifest,consent,grant,downgrade,revoke}.rs` with `pub use *::*` in `permissions/mod.rs`; move the pure manifest helpers and their tests into `manifest.rs`. No behaviour change; `command-parity-check.sh` will confirm the handler set.

findings.title: set_application_authentication validates every redirect URI but passes logout_url to Graph unchecked
findings.rationale: The front-channel logout URL is a browser redirect target with the same threat profile as a reply URL (wildcard, insecure http, javascript: scheme). A bad value today surfaces as a raw Graph 400 instead of the typed `invalid_redirect_uri` the dialog already renders for the other three fields.
findings.proposal: When `logout_url` is non-empty, run it through `validate_redirect_uri` (or a `validate_logout_url` that additionally requires an https scheme) before building the PATCH; add one test.

findings.title: Per-item loops (remove_expired_passwords, set_application_owners, initial owners) continue after a re-auth-fatal error and drop the UiError code
findings.evidence:
applications/credentials.rs:291-297
        match client.remove_password(&object_id, &cred.key_id).await {
            Ok(()) => removed_key_ids.push(cred.key_id.clone()),
            Err(err) => failures.push(KeyFailure { key_id: cred.key_id.clone(), message: err.to_string() }),
owners.rs:63-67
            Err(err) => failures.push(OwnerChangeFailure { principal_id: id.clone(), action: "add".into(), message: err.to_string() }),
dto/lib.rs:78-81  `UiError` has a session-dead reading of `REAUTH_FATAL_CODES` (`refresh_missing`, `not_signed_in`) that needs the `code`.
findings.rationale: AGENTS.md's bulk rule ("degrade to `BulkError`, stop on a re-auth-fatal code") exists because a dead refresh token cannot be re-minted silently, so every remaining item fails identically. These loops are small (one app's secrets/owners) so cancellation is not needed, but `err.to_string()` discards the code, so the frontend cannot recognise the dead session and trigger the in-place `reauthenticate`; the operator sees N identical failure strings.
findings.proposal: Convert each error with `UiError::from(err)`, carry `code` in `KeyFailure`/`OwnerChangeFailure` (additive `#[serde(default)]` field), and `break` the loop when the code is re-auth-fatal, flagging the result.

result.coverage_notes: All 15 files in the slice were read end to end: applications/{mod,cache,credentials,federated,authentication,owners,permissions_resolve}.rs and commands/{credentials,expose_api,app_roles,permissions,search,guid,progress,mod}.rs (permissions.rs in three contiguous chunks covering lines 1-1417; cache.rs in three chunks covering 1-722). Supporting files were read only in the parts needed to verify findings: state.rs (graph_for, single_flight, for_test), repo_invariants/cache.rs (session-proof and guard tests), core models.rs (Application, AppRole, ApplicationExposeApi, NewKeyCredential), azapptoolkit-dto (UiError, applications/expose_api/enterprise_application/search/permissions DTOs), graph client applications.rs/service_principals.rs/credentials.rs (signatures and cache busts), core redirect.rs/federation.rs (signatures), commands/export.rs, bulk.rs:555-600, restore.rs:210-250, and the frontend callers (create_app_dialog, home_dashboard, application_list, permission_picker, global_search, bindings/applications, util.rs). No cargo build/test/clippy/check was run per the task rules; Cargo.lock was inspected with grep/awk only. Graph API behaviour for `keyCredentials` PATCH honouring a caller-supplied `endDateTime` (finding on certificate upload) was not verified against live docs and is stated as \"nothing checks it against notAfter\" rather than as a Graph guarantee.

result.area_summary: The scoping command layer is unusually well-reasoned: the grant-scoped-before-strip ordering, the fail-closed scope-repoint guards, the AAP migration's five-step plan with its three guards, and the toolkit-managed group lifecycle all match docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md, and the pure decision logic lives in azapptoolkit-exchange with solid table tests. The weak spots are consistency at the seams: the mail-scope verdict resolver hardcodes Microsoft Graph and therefore never produces a verdict for the EWS full_access_as_app scope that every upstream gate (targets_from_declared, the frontend, the audit prefetch) treats as scopable; the permission tester's SharePoint path and the mailbox reverse lookup each have a "read failed" branch that reports definitive no-access; the site sweep's 5 000-site cap is invisible to is_complete(); and the SharePoint grant/strip steps duplicate one another and the Exchange core rather than sharing helpers as AGENTS.md implies.

findings.title: resolve_mail_scopes hardcodes Microsoft Graph, so the EWS full_access_as_app scope never gets a verdict (Permissions tab shows Unknown forever; audit scores a correctly scoped EWS app org-wide)
findings.rationale: graph_mail_role("full_access_as_app") is None, so the value is dropped in all three resolver paths. get_mail_permission_scopes emits no MailScopeEntry for it (an app declaring only the EWS scope gets an empty Vec cached without any Exchange call); get_mail_scopes_for_principal returns Unknown for it (scopes.get(&value) misses). The audit's lean resolver drops it too, so after a successful `Application EWS.AccessAsApp` scoping the audit still scores the app at org-wide weight (empty map = org-wide). The mod.rs comment justifying MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID is contradicted by the crate's own resource-aware mapping and by the repo's tests; this is not a documented decision but a regression left behind when the value-only helper was deleted.
findings.proposal: Change resolve_mail_scopes and resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached to accept the role alongside the value — e.g. `&[(String, &'static str)]` (the shape get_mail_scopes_for_principal already builds at 377-383) or `&[ExchangeTarget]` (which carries exchange_role) — and stop re-deriving the role inside. Fix the entries filter at 341 to read the role from the target rather than calling exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, ..). Update the audit caller (audit.rs:1553) to pass perms.app_role_grants' (resource, value) pairs. Correct the mod.rs:32-35 comment. Add a unit test that resolve_mail_scopes' output keys include full_access_as_app mapped to "Application EWS.AccessAsApp" and that an EWS-only input does not short-circuit before the probe. Expected effect: the EWS row shows Org-wide/Scoped like Graph rows, and the audit's reduced scoped-mail weight applies to an RBAC-scoped EWS grant.

findings.title: test_site_access claims "holds no organization-wide SharePoint grant" when the grants read actually failed
findings.rationale: When sharepoint_grants_held returns None (SP lookup or appRoleAssignments read failed), path 1 is silently skipped and, if no permission entry exists on the chain, the command returns a definitive no_access whose detail asserts a fact it never established. An app holding org-wide Sites.Read.All reads as having no access during a transient Graph failure — the exact under-report the doc forbids, and the Exchange half of the same file already avoids (RbacReach::Indeterminate).
findings.proposal: Extract the final decision into a pure fn `site_verdict(held: Option<&HeldSharePointGrants>, hit: Option<EntryHit>, label: &str) -> PermissionTestResult`; when `held.is_none()` and `hit.is_none()` return verdict "unknown" with detail "…no entry names this app…, and its app-role assignments couldn't be read, so an organization-wide grant can't be ruled out". Table-test the four combinations. Effort under an hour.

findings.title: orgwide_mailbox_grant folds a failed Graph read into EntraReach::NotHeld, yielding a definitive no_access for managed identities on a transient error
findings.rationale: Three distinct Graph failures collapse into "not held". Combined with RbacReach::None{had_assignments:false} (the managed-identity / not-in-EXO-store case, which rbac_reach_for returns for a missing-object error), synthesize produces verdict no_access and the detail states positively that no Entra grant exists. The sibling sharepoint_grants_held (884-887) explicitly distinguishes unreadable from none; the mailbox side does not. The same helper feeds the `exchange_client` failure branch (379-397) where None becomes a generic unknown, so only the main path is affected.
findings.proposal: Return a tri-state (e.g. `Result<Vec<String>, ()>` or an enum Held(Vec)/None/Unreadable) and add `EntraReach::Unreadable`, scored at level 1 (unknown) in synthesize with detail "Entra app-role assignments couldn't be read". Reuse mail_scopes::held_orgwide_mail_grants for the body (see the duplication finding) once it, too, exposes read failure. Add a synthesize test: Unreadable + RbacReach::None{false} => verdict unknown, not no_access.

findings.title: find_mailbox_reachers discovers candidates from the Microsoft Graph resource only, so an app whose sole mailbox grant is org-wide EWS full_access_as_app is missed or reported as no_access
findings.rationale: The reverse lookup answers "who can reach this mailbox?". A principal granted only full_access_as_app (full access to every mailbox over EWS) is not a Graph appRoleAssignedTo hit; if it is registered in Exchange's SP store it enters with empty held permissions and, absent an RBAC assignment, reads no_access — the strongest possible mailbox grant reported as none. The single-app tester and the audit both already close this gap, so the two surfaces disagree for the same principal.
findings.proposal: Replace graph_role_index + one appRoleAssignedTo read with mailbox_resource_roles (both resource SPs) and page list_app_role_assigned_to on each, filtering with is_scopable_exchange_resource_permission(Some(resource.app_id), value); or, simpler, reuse prefetch_ews_full_access_grants' shape to add EWS holders to `candidates` with held = ["full_access_as_app"]. Extend merge test to cover an EWS-only candidate.

findings.title: MailboxReachersResult.exchange_available can never reflect the realistic degraded mode (missing Exchange consent / 403), so the summary's partial-coverage caveat never fires
findings.rationale: For a signed-in operator with a UPN, exchange_available is always true. The doc's promised caveat is unreachable in practice.

Update the doc sentence to match.

findings.title: Site sweep silently truncates at MAX_SITES_PER_SWEEP and caches the result as complete; is_complete() has no truncation dimension (the audit result does)
findings.rationale: A tenant with more than 5 000 enumerable sites gets total_sites = 5000, sites_scanned = 5000, sites_failed = 0 → cached for 60 minutes and is_complete() = true. The per-app panel then states "no per-site grants" for an app whose grants live on site 5 001+, and the CSV coverage line claims full coverage — the exact overstatement the sweep's own comments promise never to make. Nothing tells the operator the cap was hit, so "Raise if a user legitimately hits it" can never be acted on.

result.area_summary: The SSO/rollover core is the strongest part of this slice: `build_rollover` is a pure projection of live SP state (no phase is derived from cached or local state anywhere — `get_sso_config`, `retire`, `activate`/`revert` all re-read the SP; the board is cached but rebuilt from a live filtered scan), thumbprint comparisons all route through `core::thumbprint::canonical`, the metadata parser and the phase machine are well table-tested, and the cache-busting story is honest. The weak spots are around the edges: the claims-mapping codec mis-models Graph's transformation-sourced schema entry (it emits `TransformationID` instead of the entry's own `ID` and conflates the two on read, so any transformation policy is written wrong and an existing one is corrupted on save), `set_claims_mapping` leaks one orphan `claimsMappingPolicy` per save, the create wizard silently drops a failed claims/notification step, and the managed-identity Azure RBAC view duplicates management-group-inherited assignments once per subscription while carrying a `scanned` field that is a constant alias of `total`. Conditional Access ignores workload-identity (`clientApplications`) targeting entirely, which is the CA surface most relevant to an app-registration tool. Several commands are stringly typed (`mode`, `protocol`, reason codes) and `sso/mod.rs` at 2349 lines mixes six concerns that split cleanly.

findings.title: Claims codec mis-models transformation-sourced schema entries: emits TransformationID instead of ID and conflates both on read
findings.rationale: Graph's schema entry for a transformation-sourced claim carries TWO ids: its own `ID` (which `OutputClaims[].ClaimTypeReferenceId` joins to) and `TransformationID` (which names the transformation). The DTO has one `id`, the writer emits it under `TransformationID` and omits `ID`, so every transformation policy this editor writes has an output claim with nothing to join to (the claim is never emitted). Worse, `parse_schema_entry` reads `ID` first, then `TransformationID`, into the single `id`; an existing Graph policy `{"Source":"transformation","ID":"DataJoin","TransformationID":"JoinTheData"}` parses as id="DataJoin", loses the transformation reference, and "Save claims" rewrites it as `TransformationID:"DataJoin"` — pointing at a transformation that does not exist. The round-trip test `claims_policy_round_trips_transformation` masks this by using the same string for the schema id, the transformation id and the output ClaimTypeReferenceId. Graph's own example additionally carries `"DataType":"string"` on InputParameters, which `TransformParamDto` drops on round-trip.
findings.proposal: Add `transformation_id: Option<String>` to `ClaimSchemaEntryDto`; in `build_schema_entry` always emit `ID` from `id` and emit `TransformationID` from `transformation_id` when set; in `parse_schema_entry` read `ID` and `TransformationID`/`TransformationId` into their own fields. Add `data_type: Option<String>` to `TransformParamDto` and round-trip it. Replace the masking test with one that uses Graph's documented shape (schema ID "DataJoin", TransformationID "JoinTheData", OutputClaims ClaimTypeReferenceId "DataJoin") and asserts both keys survive parse→build. Fix the DTO doc comments at sso.rs:21/33/91 and the ClaimsEditor to expose the extra field.

findings.title: set_claims_mapping leaks one orphan claimsMappingPolicy per save and swallows the listing error
findings.rationale: `remove_claims_mapping_policy` is a `$ref` DELETE — it unassigns but never deletes the tenant-level `claimsMappingPolicy` object, and every save then POSTs a fresh one via `apply_claims_policy`. A tenant accumulates one orphan under `/policies/claimsMappingPolicies` per "Save claims" click, forever, with the operator's display name on each. The comment's premise ("effectively replace-only") is wrong: Graph documents Update (PATCH) for claimsMappingPolicy, so the existing policy's `definition` can be replaced in place — no detach→assign window during which tokens carry default claims either. Separately, `if let Ok(existing)` turns a transient listing failure into an attempt to assign a second policy, which Graph rejects (one per SP) with an opaque 400.
findings.proposal: Add `update_claims_mapping_policy(id, definition_json)` (PATCH /policies/claimsMappingPolicies/{id}) and `delete_claims_mapping_policy(id)` to the graph client. In `set_claims_mapping`: propagate the listing error with `?`; if exactly one policy is assigned and the new policy is non-empty, PATCH its definition and return its id; if none, create+assign; if the new policy is empty, unassign then DELETE the policy (it was created by this tool for this SP — optionally check `appliesTo` is empty first). Document the orphan risk removed in the CHANGELOG.

findings.title: Managed-identity Azure RBAC view duplicates management-group-inherited assignments once per subscription
findings.rationale: The per-subscription `principalId eq` query returns assignments ABOVE the subscription too (management group / root). The command fans out over every reachable subscription and flattens without deduplicating, so a managed identity holding Reader at a management group over N subscriptions renders N identical rows (same `RoleAssignment.id`, same scope), each tagged with a different subscription display name. `scope_level` explicitly classifies "Management group" scopes, so these rows are expected output — and they are wrong by a factor of N. For an operator reviewing MI privilege this both inflates the count and hides the fact that it is a single inherited grant.
findings.proposal: Dedupe `flat` by `RoleAssignment.id` (fall back to `(scope, role_definition_id, principal_id)` when id is None) with a `HashSet` before role-name resolution; for an assignment whose scope is above the subscription, label `subscription` as "(inherited)" or the MG name rather than the first subscription that happened to return it. Extract a pure `dedupe_assignments(Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>) -> Vec<(String, RoleAssignment)>` and unit-test with one MG assignment returned by two subscriptions.

findings.title: AzureRolesResult.scanned is a constant alias of total; the DTO doc and the UI's "(capped)" branch are dead
findings.rationale: The cap was removed but the field survived as `scanned = total`. The DTO doc still says "(capped for safety)", and the frontend keeps a message branch ("scanned X of Y subscriptions (capped)") that can never fire. A reader of either side is told a coverage guarantee that no longer exists in the code. Since a subscription whose lookup failed is counted in `skipped`, "scanned" as a distinct number is simply `total - skipped`.
findings.proposal: Either drop `scanned` from `AzureRolesResult` (DTO + `managed_identity_detail_pane.rs` + `ipc_mock/fixtures.rs`; it is a wire-format change so note it) and let the UI render only `skipped`/`total`, or set `scanned = total - skipped`, fix the DTO doc to "subscriptions whose role-assignment lookup succeeded", and reword the UI branch. Add a one-line unit test pinning `scanned + skipped == total`.

findings.title: OIDC create leaves the client-secret lifetime unbounded, unlike the SAML cert lifetime and the rotation path
findings.rationale: `secret_lifetime_days` is caller-supplied and reaches `add_password` unchecked: `0` mints a secret that is already expired when the summary shows it; an absurd value hits Graph's rejection only AFTER `instantiate_application_template` has created the app+SP, producing exactly the half-configured app the SAML path pre-validates `cert_lifetime_days` to avoid. The sibling `rotate_app_credential` clamps to 1..=730, so the same concept has two policies in the same crate.
findings.proposal: Add `resolve_secret_lifetime_days(Option<u32>) -> Result<u32, UiError>` (typed `invalid_secret_lifetime`, bounds 1..=730 shared as a `core` constant with `keyvault.rs`), call it in `create_oidc_sso_application` before `instantiate_application_template`, and reuse the value in `configure_oidc`. One table test mirroring `a_signing_certificate_lifetime_is_bounded_by_entras_three_year_ceiling`.

findings.title: SAML create silently drops a failed claims policy or notification-email step; the wizard shows an unqualified success
findings.rationale: Degrading rather than failing is a documented decision, but the degradation is invisible: `SamlSsoSummary.claims_policy_id` is `None` on failure and nothing in the frontend reads it, so an operator who filled in the Attributes & claims step sees the same success screen as one who did not, and discovers the missing claims at the first federated sign-in. The same applies to notification emails (the "nobody is warned" column on the expiry board). `RotateCredentialResult.warnings` already establishes the pattern for exactly this situation.
findings.proposal: Add `#[serde(default)] pub warnings: Vec<String>` to `SamlSsoSummary`; in `configure_saml` push a human message on each degraded step ("Custom claims were not applied: <err>; open the SSO tab → Save claims to retry" / "Notification emails were not saved: <err>"). Render a warn `Callout` in `components/sso_summary.rs` when non-empty, and add a fixture with a warning so the GUI test covers it.

findings.proposal: Extract two pure functions next to `build_rollover`: `retire_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, key_id: &str) -> Result<&'a SigningCertDto, UiError>` and `activation_target<'a>(roll: &'a SigningCertRolloverDto, thumbprint: &str) -> Result<Option<&'a SigningCertDto>, UiError>` (None = already active, no-op). Have `retire_saml_signing_certificate` and `set_preferred_signing_key` call them. Table-test every code and both `cert_is_active` messages using the existing `sp_with`/`cred` fixtures.

findings.title: Conditional Access view ignores workload-identity targeting (conditions.clientApplications)
findings.rationale: Graph's `conditionalAccessConditionSet` also carries `clientApplications { includeServicePrincipals, excludeServicePrincipals, servicePrincipalFilter }` — workload-identity Conditional Access, which targets precisely the service principals this tool manages. The model omits it, so (a) a policy that blocks THIS app's SP is invisible if its `applications` condition names other resources, and (b) a workload-identity policy with the usual `applications.includeApplications=["All"]` is reported as "applies (all)" for every app in the tenant, whether or not its SP is the targeted client. For an app-registration/enterprise-app admin tool this is the most relevant CA dimension and it is currently mis-reported in both directions.
findings.proposal: Add `client_applications: Option<CaClientApplications>` (include/exclude SP ids, `ServicePrincipalsInMyTenant`, `servicePrincipalFilter`) to `CaConditions`. Pass the SP object id into `list_conditional_access_for_app` (the detail pane has it). In `applies_reason`, treat `excludeServicePrincipals` as exclude-wins, and when `clientApplications` is present require the SP to match (`workloadIdentity` / `workloadIdentityAll` / `workloadIdentityFilter` reason codes) before falling back to the resource-side `applications` reasons. Extend the table tests; document the codes in the DTO.

findings.title: Key Vault rotation writes secret versions with no ownership tags and no collision check
findings.rationale: `set_secret` on an existing name silently appends a version. Nothing in the written version records which app registration, object id or `keyId` it belongs to, so (1) a typo or a shared secret name across two apps overwrites another app's live secret with no warning — consumers of the old value break at their next read — and (2) an operator auditing the vault later cannot tell which app a version was minted for. The tool already knows all three identifiers at this point and already persists the vault→app binding in `UserSettings`, so the information exists; it just is not written where the vault reader can see it.
findings.proposal: Populate `tags` with `azapptoolkit-app-id`, `azapptoolkit-object-id`, `azapptoolkit-key-id` and `content_type` (e.g. `application/x-entra-client-secret`). Before `set_secret`, `get_secret(name, None)` (tolerating 404) and, if the latest version carries an `azapptoolkit-app-id` tag naming a different app, return `UiError::validation("secret_owned_by_other_app", …)` unless `input.force` is set; on the rollback path keep the existing `remove_password`. Unit-test the tag builder and the ownership predicate as pure functions.

findings.title: assign_managed_identity_azure_role never busts the Key Vault access sweep cache
findings.rationale: The sweep result is cached for the 60-minute Audit TTL and is the answer to "who can touch this vault?". A role assigned by this very app at a `/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/...` scope changes that answer, but `get_cached_key_vault_access` keeps serving the pre-assignment sweep until TTL — contradicting the repo's invalidate-on-Ok rule and the sweep's own "coverage is never overstated" stance.
findings.proposal: Make `kv_sweep_cache_key` `pub(crate)` and, on the `Ok` path of `assign_managed_identity_azure_role`, `if scope.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("/providers/microsoft.keyvault/vaults/") { state.cache.invalidate(CacheKind::Audit, &kv_sweep_cache_key(&tenant_id)); }`. Add the pairing to `repo_invariants/cache.rs` alongside the other invalidate-on-Ok pins.

findings.title: set_sso_mode / get_sso_summary are stringly typed and an unrecognised mode silently disables SSO
findings.rationale: Three string protocols (`mode`, `protocol`, `SsoConfigDto.sso_mode`) are matched by literal in both trees, and the backend's catch-all turns a casing slip ("SAML") or a future value ("password") into a destructive PATCH that clears SSO. `get_sso_summary` returns untagged `serde_json::Value` that the frontend re-branches on the same string. The repo's own convention (`CertStatus`, `RolloverPhase`) is a serde enum in `dto/sso.rs`.
findings.proposal: Add `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] enum SsoMode { Saml, Oidc, Disabled }` to `dto/sso.rs`; take it in `set_sso_mode` and `get_sso_summary` (unknown values then fail deserialization instead of clearing SSO); return `enum SsoSummary { Saml(SamlSsoSummary), Oidc(OidcSsoSummary) }` with `#[serde(tag = "protocol")]`. Update `bindings/sso.rs` (whose doc still says `""` disables) and the `<select>` in `sso_tab.rs`.

findings.title: set_sso_mode docstring says "No cache bust" while the body busts the expiry board
findings.rationale: The docstring was written before the expiry board existed and now states the opposite of both the code and the architecture doc. A reader trusting the docstring could remove the bust as "unnecessary".
findings.proposal: Replace the two docstring lines with: "Busts only the SSO-certificate expiry board (`invalidate_sso_cert_board`): the mode decides whether the app is on the board at all. The SSO tab reads the mode live and no other cached payload carries it."

findings.title: Inconsistent not-found wire codes: sso uses validation("not_found") where every other command uses UiError::not_found(resource)
findings.rationale: The same condition (SP vanished between list and detail) reaches the frontend as code `not_found` from the SSO tab and `service_principal_not_found` from the enterprise-app detail. The factory exists precisely to keep `_not_found` codes uniform; the two SSO sites predate or bypass it. Harmless today (the frontend does not branch on it) but it is the kind of drift that breaks a future `ends_with("_not_found")` handler.
findings.proposal: Replace both with `UiError::not_found("service_principal", "Service principal not found.")`. Optionally add a repo_invariants scan asserting no `UiError::validation("not_found"` / `"*_not_found"` literal exists outside the factory.

findings.title: active_thumbprint (and the board's Thumbprint column) bypass core::thumbprint::canonical
findings.evidence:
sso/mod.rs:1478-1481

        .get("preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint")
        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
        .map(str::to_string);
sso/mod.rs:1616

sso/mod.rs:1027
                thumbprint: roll.active_thumbprint,
apps/desktop/web-rs/src/views/sso_certificates_dashboard.rs:201-204

docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md: "`azapptoolkit-core::thumbprint::canonical` is the **single** converter ... every display and every comparison in both trees goes through it"
findings.rationale: `certs[].thumbprint` is canonical uppercase hex, but `active_thumbprint` is the raw `preferredTokenSigningKeyThumbprint` — which the same doc notes "can differ in case" — and it is what the expiry board prints as the app's thumbprint. On a tenant with a lowercase preferred value the board shows a lowercase string beside the SSO tab's uppercase one for the same certificate, which is exactly the operator confusion the canonical rule exists to prevent.

Extend `rollover_matches_the_preferred_thumbprint_case_insensitively_and_sorts_newest_first` to assert `roll.active_thumbprint == Some(B_HEX)` for the lowercase input.

findings.title: with_replication_retry skips steps 4 and 5 of the SAML create flow
findings.rationale: Steps 2, 3 and 5b are wrapped against the post-instantiate replication 404, but the two writes between them — the certificate POST and the activation PATCH, both against the same freshly created SP — are not. Graph front-doors are not sticky, so a request routed to a lagging replica at step 4 fails with NotFound and leaves the half-configured app the retry exists to prevent, while the cheaper best-effort step right after it would have retried.
findings.proposal: Wrap both: `with_replication_retry(|| client.add_token_signing_certificate(sp_id, &subject, end)).await?` and the step-5 PATCH. Both closures are `FnMut() -> Fut` over borrowed data, so no restructuring is needed.

findings.title: gallery partial_catalog is unreachable dead state in production
findings.rationale: The only production caller passes `false`, and the comment explains why it can never be `true` (`collect_all_pages` is all-or-nothing). The DTO field, the parameter, the `rank_gallery_propagates_partial_catalog` test and the dialog's "only partly loaded" message are leftovers from the earlier capped fetch pool. They cost a wire field on every search response and a UI branch nobody can trigger.
findings.proposal: Remove the `partial_catalog` parameter and DTO field (wire change: `GallerySearchResultsDto`, `gallery_dialog.rs`, `ipc_mock/fixtures.rs:1274/1350`), delete the dead test, and drop the dialog branch. If a partial catalog ever becomes possible again (e.g. a `SP_INDEX_MAX`-style cap on `list_all_application_templates`), reintroduce it wired to that real signal.
