result.coverage_notes: Every file in the slice was read end to end: sso/mod.rs (all 2349 lines), sso/claims.rs, enterprise_application.rs, managed_identity.rs, graph_roles.rs, gallery.rs, keyvault.rs, keyvault_rbac.rs, usage.rs, activity.rs, conditional_access.rs. Supporting code read only in the parts needed to verify findings: crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/sso.rs (full), dto/lib.rs (UiError), dto/managed_identity.rs and dto/keyvault.rs (excerpts), graph client policies.rs (full), credentials.rs / directory.rs / roles_grants.rs / service_principals.rs / applications.rs (excerpts), arm client.rs and models.rs (excerpts), core cache.rs and models.rs (excerpts), state.rs (ensure_* helpers), docs/architecture/auth-and-consent.md lines 84-340, and frontend excerpts of sso_tab.rs, sso_wizard_dialog.rs, sso_certificates_dashboard.rs, managed_identity_detail_pane.rs, gallery_dialog.rs, access.rs, bindings/sso.rs. Graph/ARM behaviour claims (claims-mapping schema, role-assignment filter inheritance, acceptMappedClaims) were verified against Microsoft Learn via the docs tool. No cargo commands were run, per the ground rules; a command-registration/binding parity scan via grep found no missing handler or stub for any command in the slice. The acceptMappedClaims requirement was investigated and found NOT to be a defect: the SSO tab and wizard offer the claims editor only for SAML apps (sso_tab.rs:722-822 `<Show when=move || is_saml>`), which always carry a custom signing certificate.

result.area_summary: The cmd-platform slice is in good shape structurally: AppState's per-tenant client memoization is one helper (`try_get_or_build`), cancellation is generation-based and well-tested, settings writes are serialized and atomic, every file the app writes goes through one owner-only choke point, the manifest carries only credential metadata, and the 186 registered commands, 186 `#[tauri::command]` fns and the frontend bindings are in exact parity (no orphans in either direction). The weak spots are (1) a documented auto-update opt-out that no code reads, (2) DR restore paths that turn a failed read into a confident "not found / not in backup" runbook line and a restore that is not idempotent while its own report tells the operator to re-run it, (3) the MI pass of the backup lacking the dead-session latch and skip-recording that passes 1-2 have, and (4) a webview trust boundary (CSP connect-src, plugin capabilities) that is wider than the frontend uses. Several doc comments have drifted from the code (pass numbering, cancel-flag "reset", settings resolution order).

findings.title: Documented auto-update opt-out (AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE / settings.json auto_update) is never read; launch check always runs
findings.evidence:
updater.rs:26-28 `pub async fn check_for_update(app: AppHandle) -> Result<Option<UpdateInfo>, UiError> {
    let updater = app.updater().map_err(updater_err)?;
    match updater.check().await.map_err(updater_err)? {`
web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:167 `if let Ok(Some(info)) = updater::check_for_update().await {` (Effect runs once on mount, unconditionally)
README.md:262-283 "To stop the checks entirely ... `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE=0` ... `{ "auto_update": false }` ... With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session."
README.md:255-259 "If you deployed the `.msi`, **disable auto-update** (see Opting out)"
crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88 `pub fn load(config_dir: &Path) -> Self { ... if let Some(env_override) = auto_update_env_override() { s.auto_update = env_override; }`
repo-wide grep for `auto_update|AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE|UserSettings::load` outside settings.rs: only README.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md hits, no Rust callers.
findings.rationale: The README and DEVELOPMENT.md promise an MDM/CI opt-out and tell MSI deployers to rely on it to avoid a second conflicting NSIS install. `UserSettings::load` (the only place the env override is applied) has no callers, and neither `check_for_update`, `perform_update` nor the frontend consult `auto_update`. An operator who set the documented switch still gets a launch-time network call and an "Update available" toast, and an MSI install can still be driven into the conflicting-install state the README warns about. A documented security/deployment control that silently does nothing is the worst kind.
findings.proposal: In `commands::updater`, gate both commands on `UserSettings::load(&crate::config_directory()).auto_update`: `check_for_update` returns `Ok(None)` (no network call) and `perform_update` returns a `UiError::validation("updates_disabled", ...)` when it is false. Surface the flag to the UI (e.g. an `updates_enabled: bool` on `AuthConfigStatus` or a tiny `get_update_policy` command) so the account menu can hide/label the manual "Check for updates" item instead of showing a confusing failure. Add a unit test on a pure `updates_enabled(settings) -> bool` helper plus a source-scanning invariant that `check_for_update` references it. Effort S.

findings.title: Restore is not idempotent, yet its own report instructs the operator to re-run it
findings.evidence:
restore.rs:748-753 `reason: format!(
    "Managed identity ({}{}) not found in the destination. Recreate it via your \
     infrastructure-as-code, then re-run the restore to re-bind its Graph \
     app-roles.",`
restore.rs:197-231 Pass 1 `for app in &backup.app_registrations { ... match create_application_core(&client, input).await { Ok(res) => { app_id_remap.insert(...); created.push(...) }` — no lookup of an existing app by name/identifier URI/marker before creating.
restore.rs:588-590 `for meta in &app.secrets { ... match client.add_password(&c.new_object_id, &name, lifetime).await {`
web-rs/src/views/dr.rs confirm modal: "This creates new app registrations in the current tenant and regenerates their secrets. It does not overwrite or delete anything that already exists."
findings.rationale: `restore_tenant` unconditionally creates a shell for every app registration in the manifest and mints fresh secrets for each. The MI runbook item explicitly tells the operator to "re-run the restore" after recreating the identities via IaC. Following that instruction duplicates every app registration (same display names, `api://` URIs rewritten to a second appId, second set of live 180-day secrets, second admin consent) in the destination tenant. There is no dry-run warning either: `plan_restore` does not look at the destination at all.
findings.proposal: Two-part fix. (1) Make the create pass adoption-aware: on creation, stamp the new application with a marker (`application.tags` supports arbitrary strings; e.g. `azapptoolkit:restored-from:{source_app_id}`), and in Pass 1 look up an existing app carrying that tag (or, failing that, same displayName + identical identifierUris) and adopt it into `app_id_remap` instead of creating; count adoptions in `RestoreReport`. (2) Have `plan_restore` query the destination for those markers and report `already_restored` so the plan view can say "N apps already exist from a previous restore and will be adopted, not recreated", and/or offer a "Re-bind managed identities only" action that runs just Pass 5. Reword the ManualItem to point at whichever path is implemented. Effort M.

findings.title: Restore reports a failed Graph read as a confident runbook fact ('not found in destination' / 'app had none in the backup')
findings.rationale: If `list_managed_identities` fails (throttled, 403 for a role that lacks directory read, or a session that died mid-restore), `unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty list and EVERY managed identity is reported as "not found in the destination — recreate via IaC", sending the infra team to recreate identities that already exist. Likewise a transient `Err` from `get_service_principal_by_app_id` is reported as "the app had none in the backup", which is false when `has_service_principal` was true. The rubric's "result that misleads the operator" case; and because these two passes never note failures on the `SessionDead` latch, a dead session in Pass 4/5 produces a full page of wrong runbook items rather than the `session_expired` flag.
findings.proposal: In `restore_managed_identities`, match on the list result: on `Err(e)` call `session.note_code(e.ui_code())` (thread `&SessionDead` into the function), push ONE `ManualItem`/warning "could not enumerate destination managed identities: {e} — re-binding skipped" and return, instead of emitting per-MI 'not found' items. In `restore_enterprise_app`, split the arm: `Ok(None)` keeps the current text, `Err(e)` pushes "could not read service principal: {e}" and notes the session code. Add the same `note_code` to the tag/patch/assign/group-member failures in that function so Pass 4 latches like Pass 2. Unit-test the MI branch with a wiremock 500 on `/servicePrincipals` asserting no per-MI 'not found' item is produced. Effort S.

findings.title: Backup Pass 3 (managed identities) is not session-latched and swallows per-MI read failures without recording them in `skipped`
findings.evidence:
backup.rs:675-683 `async fn backup_managed_identities(
    client: &GraphClient,
    managed: &[ServicePrincipal],
    cancel: &CancelToken,
    app_handle: &AppHandle,
    done: &Mutex<usize>,
    total: usize,
    throttle: &ConcurrencyThrottle,
) -> Result<Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, UiError> {` (no `session: &SessionDead`)
backup.rs:695-706 `.batch_list_app_role_assignments(&mi_ids).await
            // Per-item errors degrade to empty here (best-effort, as before);
            // only a WHOLE-batch failure takes the per-item path.
            .map(|v| v.into_iter().map(Result::unwrap_or_default).collect()),
        |id: String| async move { client.list_app_role_assignments(&id).await.unwrap_or_default() },`
Contrast backup.rs:388-391 (Pass 1) `// A DR backup that silently drops apps is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Classify every per-item failure so a dead session aborts the run instead of thinning it.
    note_graph_failures(session, app_jsons.iter().map(Result::as_ref));`
backup.rs:211-216 after Pass 2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }` — no equivalent after Pass 3.
findings.rationale: Passes 1 and 2 were hardened so a dead session aborts the backup and any dropped object lands in `TenantBackup.skipped`. Pass 3 predates that: if the refresh token dies (or Graph 5xx/429s past the retry budget) during the MI phase, every assignment read fails, is replaced with an empty `Vec`, and the run returns `Ok` — a manifest whose managed identities all have `held_app_roles: []`. Restore then re-binds nothing and reports success. The manifest neither records the gap in `skipped` nor fails, which is exactly the 'reads as complete' hazard the module documents for the other passes.
findings.proposal: Thread `session: &SessionDead` into `backup_managed_identities`; keep the per-item `Result` from `batch_or_serial`, call `note_graph_failures(session, ...)` on it, and for each `Err` push `SkippedObject::new("managedIdentity", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("held app-roles could not be read: {err}"))` while still emitting the MI with empty roles (so the operator knows the entry is partial). After the pass, mirror passes 1-2: `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err("the tenant backup")); }`. Return `(Vec<ManagedIdentityBackup>, Vec<SkippedObject>)` and append to `skipped`. Extend the existing wiremock degrade test with a 500 on `/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments` asserting the skip is recorded. Effort S.

findings.title: Enterprise-app assignee/group read failures degrade to empty with no `skipped` record — manifest silently under-reports access
findings.rationale: The whole-object skip is recorded, but a per-SP failure of `appRoleAssignedTo` or `memberOf` produces an `EnterpriseAppBackup` with zero assignees/groups and no marker. On restore the app gets no assignments re-applied and the report shows nothing amiss; users who had access in the source silently do not in the destination. The architecture doc describes the degrade, but the `skipped` mechanism was added precisely so 'degrade to empty' is never invisible; extending it here is the consistent completion of that fix, not a re-litigation.
findings.proposal: When `assigned[i]` or `groups[i]` is `Err(e)`, push `SkippedObject::new("enterpriseAppAssignments" / "enterpriseAppGroups", &sp.id, Some(sp.display_name.clone()), format!("... could not be read: {e}"))` alongside the (partial) entry. Update the `SkippedObject.kind` doc list and the arch doc sentence to say partial reads are recorded. The DR view already renders `skipped` generically. Effort S.

findings.title: Managed Identities 'Refresh' invalidates only `{tenant}|mi`, but the list is rebuilt from the untouched shared SP index — refresh is a no-op
findings.rationale: `list_managed_identities` was refactored to derive from `sp_index_cached`, but the per-page Refresh invalidation for MIs was not updated. Pressing Refresh on the Managed Identities page drops the derived `{tenant}|mi` row set, which is then immediately re-derived from the still-cached SP index — an MI created seconds ago (the common reason to press Refresh) stays absent until the SP index TTL lapses or the operator refreshes the Apps/Enterprise page instead.
findings.proposal: In the `ManagedIdentities` arm also invalidate `sp_index_key(&tenant_id)` (and `search_corpus_key`, matching the Enterprise arm's reasoning that the corpus derives from the index). Add a `repo_invariants/cache.rs` rule or a unit test asserting every `ListCacheKindDto` arm that backs a list derived from `sp_index_cached` drops the index. Effort S.

findings.title: `plan_restore` dry-run skips the schema check and omits enterprise/MI/skipped counts the restore will act on
findings.rationale: The plan is what the operator confirms against. A too-new manifest passes the dry-run and is refused only after Confirm; the plan lists app-registration work only, though Passes 4-5 will also re-apply SP settings, role assignments, group memberships and MI role re-binds; and restoring into the SOURCE tenant (which duplicates the entire estate) is the one case that shows no note, because the note is gated on `tenant_changed`.
findings.proposal: Call `check_manifest_schema` in `plan_restore` (surface as a blocker like `cloud_mismatch`). Extend `RestorePlan` (all `serde(default)`) with `enterprise_apps_to_reapply`, `enterprise_apps_manual`, `managed_identities_to_rebind`, `skipped_in_backup: usize`, and render them in `RestorePlanView`; render an explicit warning when `!tenant_changed` ("This manifest was taken from THIS tenant — restoring will create duplicates of every app"). Effort S-M.

findings.title: Restore regenerates a live 180-day secret for every backed-up password credential, including ones already expired in the source
findings.rationale: Long-lived app registrations commonly carry several expired secrets nobody rotated away. Restore turns each of them into a fresh, valid credential whose plaintext lands in the report — widening the destination tenant's credential surface beyond what was actually in use, and inflating the redistribution work. The metadata needed to distinguish them is already in the manifest.
findings.proposal: Skip secrets whose `end_date_time < Utc::now()` (and, optionally, those expiring within N days is still regenerated since it was live), pushing a warning "secret '{name}' had expired on {date} in the source and was NOT regenerated". Make `build_restore_plan` count only non-expired secrets and add `expired_secrets_skipped`. Unit-test both. Effort S.

findings.title: Webview trust boundary wider than the frontend uses: CSP connect-src lists Graph/login/Key Vault/ARM hosts and capabilities grant updater + dialog IPC the webview never calls

capabilities/default.json:6-12 `"permissions": ["core:default", "core:window:default", "core:app:default", "updater:default", "dialog:allow-save"]`

web-rs/Cargo.toml has no HTTP client (only `web-sys` features for DOM/clipboard/storage); grep of web-rs/src for `plugin:` finds only `plugin:event|listen` in ipc_mock; all updater/dialog work is backend-side (`commands::updater`, `export::write_bytes_via_dialog`).

findings.rationale: All network egress is backend reqwest; the WASM frontend only invokes custom commands and listens to events. The `connect-src` allowlist therefore protects nothing and, should the webview ever be compromised, permits it to reach Graph/login endpoints directly. `updater:default` grants `plugin:updater|check/download/install/download_and_install` to the webview, and `dialog:allow-save` grants a save dialog, neither of which the frontend uses — the backend already drives both via Rust APIs (the `pick_file` path works without any dialog grant). findings.proposal: Tighten `connect-src` to `'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost` (Tauri 2 injects its IPC origins; verify with `just dev` that invokes still flow) and drop the external hosts; remove `updater:default` and `dialog:allow-save` from `capabilities/default.json` (and the redundant `core:window:default`/`core:app:default`, already part of `core:default`), then run the GUI test shard that exercises an export to prove nothing depended on them. findings.title: rcgen `KeyPair` holds an un-zeroized copy of the PKCS#8 private key; the `zeroize` feature that fixes it is not enabled
findings.evidence:
cert.rs:106-110 `let key_pair = rcgen::KeyPair::generate_rsa_for(&rcgen::PKCS_RSA_SHA256, rcgen::RsaKeySize::_2048)...;
    // PKCS#8 PEM of the private key — surfaced once to the user, never persisted.
    let pkcs8_pem = key_pair.serialize_pem();`
cert.rs:57-63 `impl Drop for GeneratedCert { fn drop(&mut self) { self.private_key_pem.zeroize(); self.pfx_password.zeroize(); self.pfx_der.zeroize(); } }` (only the copies in GeneratedCert)
Cargo.toml:305 `rcgen = { version = "0.14", default-features = false, features = ["pem", "aws_lc_rs"] }`
rcgen-0.14.10/Cargo.toml:144-146 `[dependencies.zeroize] version = "1.2" optional = true`; rcgen-0.14.10/src/lib.rs:862-866 `#[cfg(feature = "zeroize")] impl zeroize::Zeroize for KeyPair { fn zeroize(&mut self) { self.serialized_der.zeroize(); } }`
Cargo.toml:334 `zeroize = { workspace = true }` (already a direct dep).
findings.rationale: The module promises the key does not linger on the heap, and `GeneratedCert` does wipe its PEM/PFX copies. But the source of truth — `key_pair.serialized_der` inside rcgen — is freed unwiped when `key_pair` goes out of scope at the end of `generate_self_signed`. Enabling rcgen's `zeroize` feature costs no new crate (zeroize is already in the graph) and gives a `Zeroize` impl; the caller then wipes it explicitly. (The DER copy p12-keystore takes for the bundle is a residual that upstream does not expose; worth a comment.)
findings.proposal: Add `"zeroize"` to the rcgen feature list and, in `generate_self_signed`, after `build_pfx(...)` returns, call `key_pair.zeroize()` (use `zeroize::Zeroize as _`) before it drops — e.g. bind `let mut key_pair`, or wrap in `zeroize::Zeroizing`-style scope. Document the p12-keystore residual copy beside `build_pfx`. Effort S.

findings.title: Sign-out drops only 2 of the 5 per-tenant client maps; no helper or invariant makes the sweep exhaustive
findings.rationale: No data leaks (the clients hold only an http pool + a `ScopedTokenAdapter` that re-asks the auth service, which purged the tenant's tokens), but the sweep is inconsistent and a future client map or a client that grows state (e.g. a cached ARM subscription list) would be missed. `kv_clients` is keyed per `(tenant, vault)` and only ever grows. Supporting reads outside the slice were partial and targeted: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs and private_file.rs (full), crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs (first ~140 lines plus RestorePlan/SkippedObject), commands/auth.rs sign_out only, commands/managed_identity.rs list command only, commands/applications/credentials.rs cert commands only, web-rs views/dr.rs and shell.rs excerpts, token_adapter.rs, and the vendored rcgen 0.14.10 / tauri-plugin-updater 2.12.0 sources for feature and install-path facts. I could not locate Tauri 2.11.6's `core:default` permission TOML in the registry to prove by source that it includes `core:window:default`/`core:app:default`, so that is listed as a nit on the strength of the Tauri docs only. No cargo build/test/clippy was run per instructions; the command/binding parity was checked with grep (186 registered = 186 declared, every registered name has a string literal in web-rs/src/bindings, no binding literal names an unregistered command).

result.area_summary: The invariants suite is unusually strong: rules derive their subject from a source walk (`sources::commands()`), carry vacuity floors, and self-test their detectors; IPC parity is perfect today (186 commands declared = registered = bound, every binding arg struct and return type matches its command). The weak spots are (1) nothing in CI pins that parity — only an advisory, jq-dependent PostToolUse hook that always exits 0; (2) the trust rules still check at module granularity, the one place the "helper bleed" the suite was rewritten to remove survives; (3) the DTO crate has accumulated dead schema (Key Vault set-secret types for a command that no longer exists, MI Azure-RBAC backup fields never populated, `PermissionDescriptor`), a duplicated wire type outside the crate (`DirectoryIndexStatus`), and a dozen closed-set fields typed as `String` where the crate elsewhere uses enums; and (4) a copy-paste class of bug — missing `\` continuations leaving 18-space runs inside operator-facing strings — reaches the audit export text and an SSO validation error.

verdicts.notes: Evidence is real: throttle.rs:102-103 computes `within` and then unconditionally `*last = Some(now)` BEFORE the early return at :106-109, so any 429 arriving <2s after the previous one re-anchors the window. Under a sustained storm (events every ~1s across 4-8 lanes) `within` is true for every event after the first, so the cap goes initial→initial/2 and parks there. That contradicts the module's own contract: :21 'Minimum seconds between cap halvings' and :41-42 'halves the cap ... at most once per HALVE_WINDOW_SECS' (i.e. again after the window under continued pressure), and the flooring-at-1 path the type doc describes is unreachable in the realistic shape. The only test (:232-252) fires bursts at a single instant and then advances past the window, exactly the blind spot the reviewer describes. The recovery loop (:66-70) legitimately needs `last_throttle` updated on every event for its quiet check, so the two-instant split (last_throttle vs last_halved) is the correct fix, not a hack. Impact bounded: the transport's Retry-After/retry budget still absorbs 429s at initial/2 lanes, but a storm that exhausts per-item retries becomes Transient → `unscored` → PerPrincipalScoring, so medium is fair.

Premise holds. readiness.rs:276-279 `is_graph` = write|sync|audit_log|policy|policy_write|sharepoint — no `group_membership`. capabilities.rs:308 carries `scope_feature: Some("group_membership")`, and readiness.rs:58 probes EVERY catalog `scope_feature`, so the checklist does call `probe_scope(.., "group_membership")` and takes the non-CAE branch (:286). The consuming adapter is `ScopedTokenAdapter::new_cae` (state.rs:465-468) and `ensure_group_member_token` passes cae=true (state.rs:630-636). The cache key really omits CAE-ness: token_cache.rs:127-129 keys by `(tenant_id, scope_key)`, and `access_token_inner` consults that cache first (service/mod.rs:478-488), so the non-CAE pre-warm is what the `new_cae` adapter reuses — the exact violation state.rs:563-568 spells out as MUST. Nothing pins the list (no test references `is_graph`/`probe_scope`). The extra `sync`/`policy_write` arms are dead today (no catalog entry has those scope_features) but harmless. Honest impact: a non-CAE GroupMember.ReadWrite.All token lives for one token lifetime after a readiness visit — a security-posture regression (no continuous access evaluation on a write scope), not a functional failure — so medium, not higher. Proposal (carry cae-ness next to the scope set, one table, plus a bijection test) fits the repo's 'one definition per policy' convention.

Note the existing UI wording for `skipped` ('covering grant no longer present') would itself be wrong for a veto, so a distinct reason (new field or reason string) is warranted rather than just reusing `skipped`.

Code matches: audit.rs:1489-1497 maps a lean-lookup `Err` to `None` with a warn; :1530-1545 then yields `orgwide = HashSet::new()` for the `None` arm while the Exchange probe at :1556-1565 still runs, so a `Scoped` RBAC verdict cannot be reconciled against a surviving org-wide grant; `has_admin_consent` (:1503-1505) and `sp_enabled` (:1593) also lose their input. The `Ok(None)` legit no-SP case and the `Err` case are conflated. Trigger is narrower than the tenant-wide gaps: a failed SP INDEX prefetch already yields `ServicePrincipalIndex` (:1162-1173), so this bites only when the index landed but a per-item GET fails after retries, or an app fell outside the seed cap (service_principals.rs:288-304). classify_audit_failure (:65-73) makes the `return Err` route work as proposed (non-reauth codes → Transient → PerPrincipalScoring; reauth-fatal → SessionDead). verdicts.notes: throttle.rs:102-104 sets `*last = Some(now)` unconditionally before the `within_window` early return at :106, so the anchor slides on every suppressed 429 and a stream of events spaced <2s apart never halves past the first 8→4. The struct doc at :41-43 ("halves ... at most once per HALVE_WINDOW_SECS") and the const doc at :21 ("Minimum seconds between cap halvings") both promise repeated halvings under sustained pressure, so this is a real divergence, not a documented decision. The transport fires `on_throttle` on every 429 including retries (transport.rs:626-631, batch.rs:297), which is the exact shape that keeps the window open. The only test (`on_throttle_halves_once_per_window_and_floors_at_one`, :232-252) fires bursts at one instant then advances past the window, so it cannot observe it. Consequence is bounded (the per-request Retry-After handling still works) but a cap stuck at half under a storm burns retry budget and can turn into `unscored` → degraded runs. Proposal (separate `last_halved` from `last_throttle`) is small and correct.

remediation.rs:256-264: broaders are filtered by `!broader_is_confined(...)` and an empty post-veto set hits `continue` with no `skipped.push`, contradicting the handler's own comment at :373-377 ("the value shows up in `skipped` saying so"). Could not refute; every path traced end to end reproduces the defect in the shipped build.

(1) Role mapping: crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/scoping.rs:106-116 returns Some("Application EWS.AccessAsApp") only for (OFFICE365_EXCHANGE_ONLINE_APP_ID, "full_access_as_app"); scoping.rs:77-96 graph_mail_role has no arm for it, and the crate's own test at scoping.rs:579-582 asserts exchange_role_for_resource_permission(MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID, EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP) == None. So the hardcoded MICROSOFT_GRAPH_APP_ID at apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/exchange/mail_scopes.rs:111, :242 and :341 drops the EWS value unconditionally.

(2) Declared path (app-reg Permissions tab): mail_scopes.rs:312-315 builds `scopable` from targets_from_declared, which the test at commands/exchange/tests.rs:81-105 proves yields ["Mail.Read", "full_access_as_app"] with exchange_role "Application EWS.AccessAsApp". resolve_mail_scopes then filters it out (:108-113); an EWS-only app hits `scopable.is_empty()` at :114 and returns Ok(empty) with no probe, and the entries filter at :341 emits no MailScopeEntry for it either. web-rs/src/views/tabs/permissions_tab.rs:156-161 keys the map by entry, so the EWS row misses; scope_badge.rs:35 aliases is_exchange_scopable_on to the resource-aware gate (true for EXO+full_access_as_app), so scope_cell_for:105-112 renders ScopeCell::Mailbox(Unknown) once loading ends. The result is then cached at :353 under `declared|{object_id}` until invalidate_app_details, so it is stable, not transient.

(3) Held path (enterprise app / MI pane): get_mail_scopes_for_principal's gate at :377-383 is resource-aware and keeps the EWS pair, but :426-427 passes values only into resolve_mail_scopes, which drops it; :432-435 falls back to MailPermissionScope::Unknown for that entry and caches it (:443).

(4) Audit: audit.rs:1260 pushes ResourcePermission::exchange_online(EWS_FULL_ACCESS_AS_APP) into app_role_grants, so `declared_values = perms.app_role_values()` (audit.rs:1523; core/audit/types.rs:338-343) includes it; resolve_mail_scopes_audit_cached filters it away at mail_scopes.rs:240-244 (and excludes it from the cache key). core/audit/types.rs:386-397 scope_mechanism reads mail_scopes.get(&grant.value) -> None -> full org-wide weight for an app whose only mailbox grant is an RBAC-scoped `Application EWS.AccessAsApp`. Only apply_legacy_policy_verdict (audit.rs:1585) can ever mark the EWS grant scoped, and only via a surviving legacy AAP, not RBAC.

(5) Not a documented decision: docs/architecture/exchange-scoping.md:31-33 says the probe/badge paths were meant to use the value-only role form precisely because "the two resources share no mapped value names" (i.e. EWS is unambiguous there). The value-only form was then deleted and pinned out by repo_invariants/commands.rs:129-134, and the replacement at mail_scopes.rs:101-107 / mod.rs:32-35 asserts "only Microsoft Graph's mail permissions ever are" scopable, which scoping.rs:113 and the deep-dive contradict. No unit test or repo invariant covers resolve_mail_scopes' output for the EWS value (the only resolver test, exchange/tests.rs:200-231, uses a non-mail permission), so nothing upstream or in CI prevents it.

Severity note: the audit-side error is in the conservative direction (over-reports risk, never under-reports), so there is no security exposure; the high severity rests on the Permissions tab permanently showing Unknown for the broadest mailbox grant there is and the RBAC-scoping workflow for EWS never visibly converging. remediation.rs:381-397 only passes Graph values and is unaffected. The proposal (carry the role/resource into the resolver or accept ExchangeTarget/(value, role) pairs; fix :341; correct the mod.rs comment; add a unit test) is correct and sufficient.

Reproduced by reading the full path; nothing upstream gates it. `UserSettings::load` (crates/azapptoolkit-core/src/settings.rs:82-88) is the ONLY place `auto_update_env_override()` (settings.rs:235-242) is applied, and a repo-wide grep over apps/ and crates/ for `UserSettings::load`, `.auto_update`, `AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE` finds no caller outside settings.rs's own #[cfg(test)] block. Every production reader of settings.json uses `UserSettings::stored` and reads other fields: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/state.rs:234 (client_id/tenant_id), state.rs:376 (last_account), commands/defaults.rs:19 and commands/exchange/mod.rs:74 (tenant_defaults). `commands/updater.rs:26-37` (`check_for_update`) and :44-72 (`perform_update`) call `app.updater().check()` with no policy check. The plugin is registered unconditionally at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:24 and both commands are in generate_handler at lib.rs:43-44; tauri.conf.json:45-53 has `plugins.updater.active: true` with the live GitHub `latest.json` endpoint, and capabilities/default.json:10 grants `updater:default`. The frontend fires the network check on every mount: web-rs/src/views/shell.rs:162-178 `Effect::new(... spawn_local(async { if let Ok(Some(info)) = updater::check_for_update().await { ... push_toast("Update available") }}))`, via bindings/updater.rs:11-12. Docs contradicted: README.md:262-283 ("To stop the checks entirely ... AZAPPTOOLKIT_AUTO_UPDATE=0 ... { \"auto_update\": false } ... With auto-update disabled the app makes no network calls to the updater endpoint at any point in the session"), README.md:255-259 (MSI deployers told to rely on it to avoid a conflicting NSIS install), docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:313-314. No repo invariant covers it (tests/repo_invariants/release.rs only pins version/CHANGELOG parity). The settings.rs unit tests (`settings_file_can_disable_auto_update`, :256-261) pass in isolation, so CI cannot detect the dead control. Severity stays high: it is a documented MDM/CI deployment control and a documented no-egress promise that silently does nothing in the shipped build; the one mitigating nuance is that the NSIS-over-MSI install still requires the operator to click "Update & restart", so the conflicting-install harm needs a user action, but the launch-time network call and the toast prompting that click both happen regardless of the switch.

Failing path constructed end to end. `backup_managed_identities` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/backup.rs:675-683) has no `session: &SessionDead` parameter, and `backup_tenant` calls it at :224-232 then immediately returns `Ok(TenantBackup { ... skipped })` at :234-243 with no `if session.is_dead() { return Err(session.err(..)) }` — unlike the checks after Pass 1 (:169-171) and Pass 2 (:211-213). Inside, :690-706 wraps `batch_list_app_role_assignments` with `.map(|v| v.into_iter().map(Result::unwrap_or_default).collect())` and the serial fallback with `.unwrap_or_default()`, so no `GraphError` survives to `note_graph_failures` (:342-350, used only by Pass 1 at :388-389 and Pass 2 at :541-543) and no `SkippedObject` is ever pushed for kind `managedIdentity` (the DTO explicitly reserves that kind: crates/azapptoolkit-dto/src/backup.rs:78). Trigger: a refresh-token death (or 429 past `core::http_retry` budget / 5xx) once Pass 3 begins. The token adapter surfaces as `GraphError::Token(TokenError)` (core/http_error.rs:95) whose `ui_code()` passes `refresh_missing`/`not_signed_in` through (`http_error.rs:131-133` via `reauth::passthrough_code`) — exactly the code `SessionDead::note_code` (dispatch.rs:62-64) would latch, had it been called. `batch_get_json` (graph/src/client/batch.rs:145 `chunk?`) returns whole-batch Err, `batch_or_serial` (dispatch.rs:134-160) falls to per-item `list_app_role_assignments` (graph/src/client/roles_grants.rs:36-40) which fails identically, and every MI ends with `held_app_roles: []` in an `Ok` manifest. Nothing pins this: tests/repo_invariants/fanout.rs:203-221 inspects only `dispatch_capped(` call sites, and Pass 3 deliberately uses the batch helpers' internal concurrency (backup.rs:669-672), so the rule never sees it; grep of repo_invariants/ for `batch_or_serial`, `note_graph_failures`, `backup_managed_identities` finds nothing. Downstream: `restore_managed_identities` (commands/restore.rs:769-793) iterates `mi.held_app_roles`, so an empty list yields `app_roles_rebound: 0` with zero warnings and only the unconditional Azure-RBAC `ManualItem` (:796-803) — the restore reads as a clean success. The `skipped` contract (dto/backup.rs:59-71: "A DR backup that silently drops what it could not read is the most dangerous artifact this app produces ... Restore surfaces the same list") and the DR view that renders it (web-rs/src/views/dr.rs:299-339) confirm this is the intended surfacing mechanism and that Pass 3 bypasses it. The existing wiremock test (backup.rs:1000-1127) covers only `backup_app_chunk`. Note the module comment at :693-694 ('best-effort, as before') documents the degrade, but the architecture doc (docs/architecture/backup-and-restore.md:113-116 and :101-103) claims 'a per-object failure skips just that object' and passes 1-2 were hardened after that comment was written, so this is a real inconsistency rather than a deliberate exemption. Severity high is warranted: a DR manifest that reads complete but restores no MI permissions is the hazard the module itself ranks as its worst.
